rulings.en: Air this clear should come with a warning: plans will be made.
rulings.text: Lug so skoon, jy kan amper tot môre toe sien.
rulings.back: Sky so clear you can almost see all the way to tomorrow.
flags: MISMATCH: EN joke is 'should come with a warning: plans will be made'; AF says 'you can almost see all the way to tomorrow' - a different joke, looks keyed to another line.
rulings.note: It is purposefully different because the humor reads differently in Afrikaans.

rulings.en: Sky's doing the most, but only a little.
rulings.text: Die lug wen, maar dis nie veel van n kompetisie nie.
rulings.back: The sky wins, but it's not much of a competition.
flags: MISMATCH: EN 'Sky's doing the most, but only a little' (extra, but barely); AF 'Die lug wen, maar dis nie veel van n kompetisie nie' (the sky wins, not much of a competition) is a different joke - looks keyed to another line; also 'n typo.

rulings.en: The sky just went full Carte Blanche.
rulings.text: Die lug het voluit bedonerd gegaan.
rulings.back: The sky has gone full-on grumpy.
flags: MISMATCH: EN 'went full Carte Blanche' (TV-exposé drama) became 'voluit bedonerd gegaan' (gone full-on grumpy) — a different joke with the Carte Blanche reference gone; 'bedonerd' is also misspelt (bedonnerd)

rulings.en: Nobody told the forecast. It just arrived.
rulings.text: Niemand het die voorspelling gesê nie. Dit het net opgedaag.
rulings.back: Nobody said the forecast. It just showed up.
flags: MISMATCH: EN 'Nobody told the forecast' needs 'vir die voorspelling gesê'; 'Niemand het die voorspelling gesê nie' reads as the garbled 'nobody said the forecast', so the forecast-wasn't-informed joke is gone
rulings.note: Cahnge it to Niemand het die voorspelling genooi nie. Dit het net opgedaag.

rulings.en: Clouds today, vibes optional.
rulings.text: Windgat wolke vandag.
rulings.back: Show-off clouds today.
flags: MISMATCH: 'Windgat wolke' (show-off, cocky clouds) is a different joke, the opposite of the laid-back 'vibes optional', and the 'wind' in 'windgat' suggests the wrong condition.
rulings.note: You are taking the wind in windgat to literal.

rulings.en: Clear sky, clear diary. One of those is a lie.
rulings.text: Nul wolke. Nul verskonings. Nul kans dat ek binne bly.
rulings.back: Zero clouds. Zero excuses. Zero chance I'm staying inside.
flags: MISMATCH: A different joke: the English 'Clear sky, clear diary. One of those is a lie.' says the diary isn't clear, while 'Nul wolke. Nul verskonings. Nul kans dat ek binne bly.' is a no-excuses, going-outside line. It looks keyed to another line.
WRONG SOURCE? The back-translation is closer to another line of the same bin: "Not a cloud in sight. Not one."

rulings.en: Golden hour runs daily. Attendance still somehow optional.
rulings.text: Goue uur: elke dag gratis, en ons is elke dag weer verbaas.
rulings.back: Golden hour: free every day, and every day we're amazed all over again.
flags: MISMATCH: The English dig 'Attendance still somehow optional' (people skip it) becomes 'ons is elke dag weer verbaas' (we're amazed every day), close to the opposite point.
rulings.note: Golden hour is a dawn or dusk thing. Not for day.

rulings.en: Mixed bag out there. We're hedging.
rulings.text: Gemengde sak daar buite. Ons hou voor.
rulings.back: Mixed bag out there. We're holding back / reserving...
flags: MISMATCH: 'Ons hou voor' is garbled Afrikaans. It does not say 'We're hedging', or anything clear, so the punchline is lost.
rulings.note: This is very hard to translate. Might need a new Afrikaans line.

rulings.en: The sun woke up and chose glorious.
rulings.text: Vandag se son het opgedaag met attitude.
rulings.back: Today's sun showed up with attitude.
flags: DRIFT: EN meme punchline 'woke up and chose glorious' is gone; 'opgedaag met attitude' (showed up with attitude) reads sassy rather than glorious.
WRONG SOURCE? The back-translation is closer to another line of the same photograph: "The Helderberg is showing off today."

rulings.en: Sun, hide-and-seek champion of the day.
rulings.text: Die lug speel kat en muis.
rulings.back: The sky is playing cat and mouse.
flags: DRIFT: EN 'Sun, hide-and-seek champion of the day'; AF 'Die lug speel kat en muis' switches subject to the sky, swaps the game and drops 'champion'.
WRONG SOURCE? The back-translation is closer to another line of the same photograph: "Sky's doing the most, but only a little."
rulings.note: Try Die son en die wolke speel kat en muis vandag.

rulings.en: Zero mistakes from today so far. Sky included.
rulings.text: Die dag het nog niks verkeerd gedoen nie. Gee hom kans.
rulings.back: The day hasn't done anything wrong yet. Give it a chance.
flags: DRIFT: 'Sky included' is dropped, and 'Gee hom kans' (give it a chance) puts a new, faintly wary kicker on what the English makes pure praise.
WRONG SOURCE? The back-translation is closer to another line of the same bin: "If you're inside, you're doing it wrong."
rulings.note: Just try Die dag het nog niks verkeerd gedoen nie. En wil ook nie.

rulings.en: Inbox: 47. Sky: flawless. Priorities: sorted.
rulings.text: Eerste koffie buite. Die e-posse kan wag.
rulings.back: First coffee outside. The emails can wait.
flags: DRIFT: The 'Inbox: 47. Sky: flawless. Priorities: sorted.' list gag becomes 'Eerste koffie buite. Die e-posse kan wag.', which adds coffee and drops the 47 and the sky.
WRONG SOURCE? The back-translation is closer to another line of the same bin: "Take your coffee outside. You deserve it."

rulings.en: The sun took its time this morning. Worth the wait.
rulings.text: Die son vat sy tyd vanoggend, en dit wys.
rulings.back: The sun's taking its time this morning, and it shows.
flags: DRIFT: EN payoff 'Worth the wait' is lost; 'en dit wys' (and it shows) makes the slow sun sound sluggish, flipping the positive note.
rulings.note: Die son vat sy tyd vanoggend, en dit is 100% dit werd.

rulings.en: Enjoy it. There's a cold front out there doing warm-ups.
rulings.text: Geniet dit. Die koue front het klaar sy tasse gepak.
rulings.back: Enjoy it. The cold front has already packed its bags.
flags: DRIFT: EN 'a cold front out there doing warm-ups' (coming); 'het klaar sy tasse gepak' can easily read as the front having already left, the opposite claim.
rulings.note: Geniet dit. Erens daarbuite is n kouefront besig om planne te maak.

rulings.en: Even Monday looks photogenic in this light.
rulings.text: Oggendson wat só lyk maak selfs Maandag draaglik.
rulings.back: Morning sun that looks like this makes even Monday bearable.
flags: DRIFT: EN says Monday 'looks photogenic in this light'; AF says morning sun makes Monday 'draaglik' (bearable) - different claim, photo joke lost.

rulings.en: The moon's doing the most tonight.
rulings.text: Die maan doen sy bes vanaand.
rulings.back: The moon is doing its best tonight.
flags: DRIFT: EN slang 'doing the most' (showing off, extra) became 'doen sy bes' (doing its best), which reads as effort/trying, not excess.

rulings.en: Cancel everything. This is THE day winter was hiding.
rulings.text: Kanselleer alles. Dis DIÉ dag.
rulings.back: Cancel everything. It's THE day.
flags: DRIFT: EN 'THE day winter was hiding' - the winter/season hook is dropped; AF is just 'Dis DIÉ dag'.
rulings.note: Kanselleer alles. Winter gee jou n blaaskans vandag.

rulings.en: Africa showing off again. Quietly devastating.
rulings.text: Afrika pronk weer. Dit mag maar.
rulings.back: Africa's showing off again. It's allowed.
flags: DRIFT: EN punchline 'Quietly devastating' replaced by 'Dit mag maar' (it's allowed) - different, flatter payoff.

rulings.en: The sun hit snooze again. Honestly? Same.
rulings.text: Die son het snooze gedruk. Weer.
rulings.back: The sun hit snooze. Again.
flags: DRIFT: EN relatable punchline 'Honestly? Same.' is dropped; AF stops at 'Weer.' (Again).

rulings.en: 50/50 on getting wet. Like a coin toss.
rulings.text: 50/50 kans om nat te word. Better odds as om die Lotto te wen...
rulings.back: 50/50 chance of getting wet. Better odds than winning the Lotto...
flags: DRIFT: EN punchline 'Like a coin toss' replaced by 'Better odds as om die Lotto te wen' - different gag (reads like another variant) with a half-English phrase.

rulings.en: Some clouds. Some sun. South African summer admin.
rulings.text: Sonnig met n spatsel wolke. SA somer in een prentjie.
rulings.back: Sunny with a sprinkle of clouds. SA summer in one picture.
flags: DRIFT: EN 'South African summer admin' punchline lost; AF 'SA somer in een prentjie' (SA summer in one picture) is a different, flatter close; also 'n typo.

rulings.en: Cloudy enough to comment, sunny enough to ignore.
rulings.text: Bewolk genoeg om te kla, sonnig genoeg om jou te maak hoop.
rulings.back: Cloudy enough to complain, sunny enough to make you hope.
flags: DRIFT: EN 'sunny enough to ignore' became 'sonnig genoeg om jou te maak hoop' (sunny enough to make you hope) - second half of the claim changed.

rulings.en: Washing's still safe. Probably.
rulings.text: Wasgoed is veilig. Hopelik.
rulings.back: Washing is safe. Hopefully.
flags: DRIFT: The brand hedge "Probably" became "Hopelik" (hopefully), and "still" is dropped; the canon uses "waarskynlik" for this hedge.

rulings.en: The sky can't make up its mind. Join the club.
rulings.text: Die lug kan nie besluit nie. Tipies.
rulings.back: The sky can't decide. Typical.
flags: DRIFT: Punchline changed: the self-deprecating "Join the club" became "Tipies" (typical), which is exasperation instead of fellow feeling.

rulings.en: Somebody left the freezer door open overnight.
rulings.text: Die Karoo het die verkoeler oopgelos.
rulings.back: The Karoo left the cooler open.
flags: DRIFT: A place is added and the subject changes: "Somebody left the freezer door open overnight" became "Die Karoo het die verkoeler oopgelos". "verkoeler" can also read as a car radiator, and "overnight" is dropped.
rulings.note: Die Karoo het die yskas oornag oopgelos.

rulings.en: Looks like a tourism ad. Feels like the inside of a fridge.
rulings.text: Joburg lyk soos 'n advertensie en voel soos 'n yskas.
rulings.back: Joburg looks like an advert and feels like a fridge.
flags: DRIFT: A place is added: the English has no city, but the Afrikaans opens with "Joburg". "tourism ad" is flattened to "advertensie" and "the inside of" is dropped.

rulings.en: That first breath of air will wake you better than coffee.
rulings.text: Daai eerste asemteug gaan jou wakker maak. Belowe.
rulings.back: That first breath is going to wake you up. Promise.
flags: DRIFT: Punchline lost: "will wake you better than coffee" became "gaan jou wakker maak. Belowe." (will wake you up. Promise.), so the coffee comparison is gone.

rulings.en: Even the dog's breath is showing. That's the reading.
rulings.text: Die hond se asem wys ook. Dis hoe koud dit is.
rulings.back: The dog's breath shows too. That's how cold it is.
flags: DRIFT: Punchline flattened: "That is the reading" (the dog as thermometer) became the plain "Dis hoe koud dit is" (that is how cold it is).

rulings.en: Tomorrow's first task: five minutes of windscreen scraping in your work clothes.
rulings.text: Môreoggend se eerste taak: vyf minute ys krap in jou kerkklere.
rulings.back: Tomorrow morning's first job: five minutes of scraping ice in your church clothes.
flags: DRIFT: "in your work clothes" became "in jou kerkklere" (church clothes), which makes tomorrow a Sunday instead of a workday. That changes the day.

rulings.en: Shorts weather? This is underwear weather.
rulings.text: Kortbroekie weer? Dis onderbroekie weer.
rulings.back: Shorts weather? It's undies weather.
flags: DRIFT: Split compounds 'Kortbroekie weer? ... onderbroekie weer' let 'weer' read as 'again' ('Shorts again? It's undies again'); solid 'kortbroekieweer / onderbroekieweer' keeps the weather joke.
rulings.note: Change it to Kortbroek weer, kortbroekie also sounds like underwear.

rulings.en: The clouds are having a moment.
rulings.text: Die wolke het 'n oomblik.
rulings.back: The clouds are having a moment.
flags: DRIFT: 'Die wolke het 'n oomblik' is a word-for-word calque of 'having a moment'; the idiom does not exist in Afrikaans (af-voice anti-pattern 1 names this exact line).
rulings.note: Change it to Die wolke tjank, iemand kry n tissue asb.

rulings.en: Night rain maths: half the visibility, double the concentration, triple the respect.
rulings.text: Nagreënwiskunde: helfte die sig, dubbel die konsentrasie, drie keer die respek.
rulings.back: Night-rain maths: half the visibility, double the concentration, three times the respect.
flags: DRIFT: 'helfte die sig' is an English calque of 'half the visibility' (Afrikaans: 'half die sig'); reads machine-made in an otherwise chatty line.

rulings.en: Unplug the things. The sky has plans.
rulings.text: Skakel jou toestelle af. Die lug het planne.
rulings.back: Switch off your devices. The sky has plans.
flags: DRIFT: EN says unplug ('Unplug the things'); 'Skakel jou toestelle af' says switch off, which drops the lightning-safety point.

rulings.en: The sky just went full Carte Blanche.
rulings.text: Die lug het voluit bedonnerd gegaan.
rulings.back: The sky has gone full-on bedonnerd.
flags: DRIFT: The SA anchor 'full Carte Blanche' (TV show / free-rein pun) is replaced by a thunder pun ('bedonnerd'); claim still 'sky went all-out' but the reference is gone.

rulings.en: The braai cover is in the next suburb.
rulings.text: Die braai-deksel is in die volgende voorstad.
rulings.back: The braai lid is in the next suburb.
flags: DRIFT: EN 'braai cover' (fabric cover) became 'braai-deksel' (braai lid) — a different object, may not match the photo; 1339 used 'oortreksel' for cover

rulings.en: Thunder's grumbling, hey.
rulings.text: Die donder dreun.
rulings.back: The thunder rumbles.
flags: DRIFT: chatty EN 'Thunder's grumbling, hey.' became the flat, formal 'Die donder dreun.' — spoken 'hey' dropped, reads like a textbook sentence

rulings.en: In the Karoo this isn't rain. It's a celebrity appearance.
rulings.text: In die Karoo is dit nie reën nie. Dis 'n verskyning.
rulings.back: In the Karoo it isn't rain. It's an apparition.
flags: DRIFT: EN 'a celebrity appearance' shrank to 'n verskyning' (an appearance/apparition) — the celebrity punchline is lost
rulings.note: Change last line to Dis vroee Kersfees,

rulings.en: Theewaterskloof is about to trend in the group chat.
rulings.text: Theewaterskloof gaan vanoggend viraal in die groepsgesprek.
rulings.back: Theewaterskloof is going viral in the group chat this morning.
flags: DRIFT: adds a time of day: 'vanoggend' (this morning) is not in EN 'is about to trend in the group chat'

rulings.en: Post-storm Highveld air should be bottled and sold overseas.
rulings.text: Die Hooglandlug ná reën behoort in 'n botteltjie verkoop te word.
rulings.back: The highland air after rain should be sold in a little bottle.
flags: DRIFT: EN 'Highveld' became 'Hoogland' (reads as generic highlands, not Hoëveld), and 'sold overseas' lost 'overseas', flattening the export boast

rulings.en: One drought in living memory and now every downpour is a lottery win.
rulings.text: Drie jaar se droogte-geheue en skielik is elke bui 'n lotto-wen.
rulings.back: Three years of drought memory and suddenly every shower is a lotto win.
flags: DRIFT: adds a number: EN 'One drought in living memory' became 'Drie jaar se droogte-geheue' (three years of drought memory)

rulings.en: All plans are officially moved to 'when it clears up'. Which is never. Shame.
rulings.text: Alle afsprake is amptelik verskuif na 'wanneer dit opklaar'.
rulings.back: All appointments are officially moved to 'when it clears up'.
flags: DRIFT: the kicker 'Which is never. Shame.' is dropped, so the line ends on the setup; 'plans' also became 'afsprake' (appointments)

rulings.en: The Boland is getting watered in its sleep and will absolutely brag about it tomorrow.
rulings.text: Die Boland word in sy slaap natgelê en môre spog hy daaroor.
rulings.back: The Boland is getting soaked in its sleep and tomorrow it'll brag about it.
flags: DRIFT: EN 'getting watered in its sleep' became 'word in sy slaap natgelê' — 'natlê' means bed-wetting, so the Boland now wets the bed and brags about it, a cruder image than being watered

rulings.en: Not depressing. Just... underwhelming.
rulings.text: Nie depressief nie. Net...grys.
rulings.back: Not depressed. Just... grey.
flags: DRIFT: punchline 'underwhelming' became a literal 'grys', and 'depressief' means depressed rather than EN 'depressing'

rulings.en: The sky picked a vibe and the vibe is shrug.
rulings.text: Die lug het n vibe gekies en die vibe is slapgat.
rulings.back: The sky picked a vibe and the vibe is slapgat — lazy and useless.
flags: DRIFT: EN 'the vibe is shrug' (mild indifference) became 'slapgat' (slack-arsed, lazy), which is cruder and more insulting; 'n' is also missing its apostrophe

rulings.en: The day is ending like a voicenote that just cuts off mid-
rulings.text: Die dag eindig soos 'n voicenote wat net skielik ophou.
rulings.back: The day ends like a voice note that just suddenly stops.
flags: DRIFT: in EN the line itself cuts off ('cuts off mid-'); AF 'wat net skielik ophou' only describes the cut-off, so the visual gag is gone

rulings.en: Sky's drafting, not committing.
rulings.text: Die lug will will, maar wil ook nie.
rulings.back: The sky sort-of wants to, but also doesn't want to.
flags: DRIFT: The claim (sky can't commit) survives, but 'will will' is English spelling (typo for 'wil-wil') and reads broken; the 'drafting' image is gone.

rulings.en: Clouds, but make it casual.
rulings.text: Net n halwe koppie wolke vir vandag se resep.
rulings.back: Just half a cup of clouds for today's recipe.
flags: DRIFT: The joke is rebuilt as a recipe ('halwe koppie wolke ... resep') in place of 'but make it casual'. The claim of light cloud survives. 'n' is missing its apostrophe.

rulings.en: The sky's doing freelance today.
rulings.text: Lug doen afskeep werk.
rulings.back: Sky's doing a slapdash job.
flags: DRIFT: 'afskeep werk' (slapdash, shoddy job) swaps the part-time 'freelance' joke for a poor-quality judgement.

rulings.en: Karoo white noise: one windpump, no off switch.
rulings.text: Plattelandse wit-geraas: een windpomp, geen af-knoppie.
rulings.back: Platteland white noise: one windpump, no off button.
flags: DRIFT: The place is generalised: 'Karoo white noise' becomes 'Plattelandse wit-geraas' (countryside).

rulings.en: The front left. The cold just moved in permanently.
rulings.text: Die front is weg. Die koue het net getrek, nie geloop nie.
rulings.back: The front is gone. The cold only moved house, it didn't leave.
flags: DRIFT: 'Die koue het net getrek, nie geloop nie' is ambiguous (moved house vs moved off) and loses the clear 'moved in permanently'.

rulings.en: Snow on the mountains means socks in bed. That's the law.
rulings.text: Sneeu op die berge beteken sokkies in die bed.
rulings.back: Snow on the mountains means socks in bed.
flags: DRIFT: The kicker 'That's the law.' is dropped, leaving a flat statement.

rulings.en: Snow on those mountains, ice in this breeze. Connected? Very.
rulings.text: Sneeu op daai berge, ys in hierdie briesie.
rulings.back: Snow on those mountains, ice in this breeze.
flags: DRIFT: The punchline 'Connected? Very.' is dropped, so the line stops before its joke.

rulings.en: The sea is sparkling like holidays. The air says otherwise.
rulings.text: Die see blink soos vakansie. Die wind chill sê andersins.
rulings.back: The sea sparkles like a holiday. The wind chill says otherwise.
flags: DRIFT: 'Die wind chill' adds wind where the English says 'the air' (a cold-clear line, not a wind one).

rulings.en: Mzansi winter does colour like nobody else. Warmth, though...
rulings.text: Winter in Mzansi doen kleur soos niemand anders nie.
rulings.back: Winter in Mzansi does colour like nobody else.
flags: DRIFT: The turn 'Warmth, though...' is dropped, so a backhanded joke becomes a plain compliment.

rulings.en: The view is free. So is the feeling in your ears — gone.
rulings.text: Die uitsig is gratis. Die gevoel in jou ore ook weg.
rulings.back: The view is free. The feeling in your ears also gone.
flags: DRIFT: The 'free' pun is lost and the second sentence has no verb ('Die gevoel in jou ore ook weg'), so 'ook' points at nothing. It reads half-built.

rulings.en: Joburg sunsets are winter's consolation prize. It's a good prize.
rulings.text: Joburg se sonsondergange is winter se troosprys.
rulings.back: Joburg's sunsets are winter's consolation prize.
flags: DRIFT: The warm tag 'It's a good prize.' is dropped, which leaves the backhanded half only.

rulings.en: The city only looks this sharp when it genuinely hurts outside.
rulings.text: So helder sien jy Kaapstad net wanneer dit regtig seer is buite.
rulings.back: You only see Cape Town this clearly when it's really bitter outside.
flags: DRIFT: Adds a place: English 'The city' becomes 'Kaapstad'.

rulings.en: Karoo night fog: rare enough that it'll get mentioned in church on Sunday.
rulings.text: Karoo-nagmis: so skaars dat die dominee dit môre gaan noem.
rulings.back: Karoo night mist: so rare the dominee is going to mention it tomorrow.
flags: DRIFT: 'môre' (tomorrow) replaces 'on Sunday'. The day changes, and the line only holds on a Saturday night.

rulings.en: This is the stuff. Right here.
rulings.text: Hierdie is die weer wat ons wil he. Net soos dit is.
rulings.back: This is the weather we want. Just as it is.
flags: DRIFT: The chatty 'This is the stuff. Right here.' is flattened to a literal 'Hierdie is die weer wat ons wil he. Net soos dit is.', and 'he' needs its diacritic ('hê').

rulings.en: Feels like the country is on its best behaviour.
rulings.text: Voel of die weer op sy beste gedrag is.
rulings.back: Feels like the weather is on its best behaviour.
flags: DRIFT: 'die weer' replaces 'the country', which loses the joke that the country itself is behaving.

rulings.en: This is leave-form weather and HR knows it.
rulings.text: Weer soos dié vra mooi vir 'n verlofvorm.
rulings.back: Weather like this is practically begging for a leave form.
flags: DRIFT: The kicker 'and HR knows it' is dropped. 'vra mooi vir 'n verlofvorm' keeps only the leave-form idea.

rulings.en: 'Quick dip before work.' Nobody in history has been quick.
rulings.text: Nog 'n 'vinnige swem voor werk' — die Kaap se oudste leuen.
rulings.back: Another 'quick swim before work' - the Cape's oldest lie.
flags: DRIFT: The joke is rebuilt from 'Nobody in history has been quick' into 'die Kaap se oudste leuen', which adds a Cape place anchor the English does not have.

rulings.en: Highveld mornings: freezing, gorgeous, zero apologies.
rulings.text: Hoëveld-oggend: koud genoeg vir 'n jas, mooi genoeg dat jy nie omgee nie.
rulings.back: Highveld morning: cold enough for a coat, pretty enough that you don't mind.
flags: DRIFT: The 'zero apologies' punchline becomes 'mooi genoeg dat jy nie omgee nie', 'freezing' softens to 'koud genoeg vir 'n jas', and the line is longer than the English.

rulings.en: Signal: weak. Views: unfair. Deadlines: whose?
rulings.text: Berg-oggende laat jou vergeet wat 'n deadline is.
rulings.back: Mountain mornings make you forget what a deadline is.
flags: DRIFT: 'Signal: weak. Views: unfair.' is dropped and the line is rebuilt around 'Berg-oggende', adding a morning; only the deadline idea survives.

rulings.en: Atlantic rule: the water is freezing and everyone lies about it.
rulings.text: Die water is yskoud en almal maak of dit lekker is. Tradisie.
rulings.back: The water is ice-cold and everyone pretends it's lekker. Tradition.
flags: DRIFT: 'Atlantic rule' is dropped, so the place is lost. 'maak of dit lekker is' for 'lies about it' is fine.

rulings.en: You don't waste a sky like this on being sensible.
rulings.text: Sonskyn soos dié los jy nie vir Maandag nie.
rulings.back: Sunshine like this you don't save for Monday.
flags: DRIFT: Adds a weekday, 'los jy nie vir Maandag nie' (you don't leave it for Monday), where the English has none, and drops the 'being sensible' joke. It reads wrong on a Monday photograph.

rulings.en: Karoo sky: same flawless blue for the next 400 km. Guaranteed.
rulings.text: Karoo-blou: presies dieselfde perfekte kleur van hier tot môre.
rulings.back: Karoo blue: exactly the same perfect colour from here to tomorrow.
flags: DRIFT: 'for the next 400 km' becomes 'van hier tot môre', turning distance into time, and 'Guaranteed' is dropped.

rulings.en: Padkos hits different under infinite sky. That's just science.
rulings.text: Padkos smaak beter onder 'n lug sonder einde.
rulings.back: Padkos tastes better under a sky without end.
flags: DRIFT: The kicker 'That's just science' is dropped, leaving a plain statement.

rulings.en: A day so good even rush hour felt optional.
rulings.text: Die dag was so mooi, selfs die verkeer het saamgespeel.
rulings.back: The day was so lovely even the traffic played along.
flags: DRIFT: 'even rush hour felt optional' becomes 'selfs die verkeer het saamgespeel' (even the traffic cooperated), a different claim.

rulings.en: City folk pay good money for this ceiling.
rulings.text: Stadsmense betaal groot geld hiervoor. Hier's dit sommer verniet.
rulings.back: City people pay big money for this. Here it's just free.
flags: DRIFT: 'this ceiling' (the sky as a ceiling) flattens to 'hiervoor', and an explanatory 'Hier's dit sommer verniet' is added.

rulings.en: Nobody's called it a night. The night agrees.
rulings.text: Niemand het 'huis toe' gesê nie. Niemand gaan ook nie.
rulings.back: Nobody's said 'home time'. Nobody's going either.
flags: DRIFT: The punchline 'The night agrees' is replaced by 'Niemand gaan ook nie' (nobody's going either).

rulings.en: The frogs have entered the chat.
rulings.text: Die paddas het die gesprek betree.
rulings.back: The frogs have entered the chat.
flags: DRIFT: 'die gesprek betree' is a stiff, word-for-word calque of 'entered the chat', and the meme register does not carry over.

rulings.en: Models say lovely. Reality reserves the right to differ.
rulings.text: Modelle sê pragtig. Die werklikheid hou voor om te verskil.
rulings.back: Models say gorgeous. Reality reserves the right to differ.
flags: DRIFT: 'hou voor om te verskil' is a broken calque of 'reserves the right to differ' (it needs 'behou die reg voor'). The meaning only comes through from context.

rulings.en: Cloud's the call. With an asterisk.
rulings.text: Wolk is die roep. Met 'n sterretjie.
rulings.back: Cloud is the call. With an asterisk.
flags: DRIFT: 'Wolk is die roep' calques 'the call' in the sense of a decision, but Afrikaans 'roep' reads as a cry or summons.

rulings.en: Might spit a bit. Might not bother.
rulings.text: Mag n bietjie spoeg. Mag dalk nie moeite doen daarmee nie.
rulings.back: Might spit a bit. Might not bother with it.
flags: DRIFT: The English-shaped 'Mag ... Mag dalk nie moeite doen daarmee nie' (mag = may, be allowed to) is stiff and longer than 'Might not bother', and 'n' is missing its apostrophe.

rulings.en: Chilly, most likely. Layer up to be safe.
rulings.text: Koel, heel waarskynlik. Trek aan om veilig te wees.
rulings.back: Cool, most likely. Dress up to be safe.
flags: DRIFT: 'Trek aan om veilig te wees' means 'get dressed to be safe', not 'layer up', and reads as a stiff calque; 'Koel' is also milder than 'Chilly'.

rulings.en: Calm night, most likely. The sky reserves the right to change.
rulings.text: Kalm nag, heel waarskynlik. Die lug hou voor om te verander.
rulings.back: Calm night, most likely. The sky reserves the right to change.
flags: DRIFT: 'hou voor om te verander' is a broken calque of 'reserves the right to change'. The meaning only comes through from context.
